commit_subject: ground policy surfaces in ingested sources
description: carer's allowance and carer support payment with the 35-hour and £204 earnings conditions

release_errors_before_success.error: No active corpus source found for 'uk/guidance/govuk/carers-allowance/eligibility'

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module paid carer's allowance whenever the person met the 35-hour test or had a reported carer's allowance amount, omitting the GOV.UK eligibility conditions that the carer be 16 or over, not in full-time education, caring for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit, and earning £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read: the vendored slice uk/guidance/govuk/carers-allowance/eligibility says "All of the following must apply: You're 16 or over. You're not in full-time education. You're not studying for 21 hours a week or more. Your earnings are £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses." - so the added conditions are source-required. Same pattern as index 0, including the co-occurring untraceable `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` disjunct that the fix removes. Residual gap after the fix: the "not studying for 21 hours a week or more" condition is still unencoded. The Scotland carve-out was kept but re-expressed (`not person_lives_in_scotland` replacing the `carer_support_payment_replaces_carers_allowance` switch). Boundary: source "£204 or less" vs encoded <= 204 - consistent.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned-release text of the cited provision (uk/guidance/govuk/carers-allowance/eligibility) states "All of the following must apply: You're 16 or over. You're not in full-time education. ... Your earnings are £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses", yet the pre-fix formula paid the full annual rate on a 35-hour-or-reported-receipt gate alone, so the encoding disagreed with the source it already cited in module.source_verification and in its proof atoms. The fix adds a new derived rule entitled_to_carers_allowance conjoining age 16+, the qualifying disability benefit of the person cared for, the new £204 carers_allowance_weekly_earnings_limit parameter, and not-in-full-time-education, and gates the weekly/annual amounts on it — an encoded-meaning change, corroborated by the companion test where a carer earning 250 a week now yields 0 instead of 4495.40. The competing kind untraceable_branch is genuinely present (the fix also deletes the ungrounded "or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0" disjunct whose rule source was "PolicyEngine UK carers_allowance final receipt wrapper"), but it covers one removed disjunct while four source-stated conditions were added, and the commit/PR text foregrounds "the 35-hour and £204 earnings conditions", so unrepresented_clause remains the better fit.

triage.verifier_notes:
Source text resolved through the pinned release (corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-07-12, record 373652ec-a2f1-5bd8-ac3b-28c509ec0701) reads: "You could get £86.45 a week if you care for someone at least 35 hours a week and they get certain benefits. ... All of the following must apply: You're 16 or over. You're not in full-time education. You're not studying for 21 hours a week or more. Your earnings are £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses. If you live in Scotland, you need to apply for Carer Support Payment instead of Carer's Allowance." Note fix_time_corpus_match = provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref, i.e. the slice was vendored in this same commit, so the pre-fix module cited a path whose text was not yet in-repo — that weakens but does not defeat the fidelity reading, because the pre-fix module already listed that citation path and quoted it in proof atoms.

Refutation lines I considered and rejected: (1) "new coverage the module never claimed" — the pre-fix summary self-describes as "This PolicyEngine-alignment surface", which is the strongest not_a_defect argument, but the rule outputs carers_allowance_annual_amount and justifies its gate with proof atoms from the eligibility page, so it did claim to encode that source and contradicted it; (2) mechanical — refuted by the test diff, where the deleted case england_reported_receipt_preserves_award asserted 4495.40 for a person with weekly_care_hours: 0.

For the reviewer: this diff carries a second, co-present defect signature — removal of the untraceable "or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0" disjunct (source line changed from "PolicyEngine UK carers_allowance final receipt wrapper" to "GOV.UK, Carer's Allowance, \"Eligibility\"") — so if the corpus wants one defect per kind, this commit could legitimately be counted under untraceable_branch as well. Also incidental and not part of the claimed defect: effective_from moves from '2026-04-06' to '0001-01-01' on three rules (timeless encoding, arguably a regression in the wrong_period_or_effective_date direction), and the post-fix module still omits the source's "You're not studying for 21 hours a week or more" condition, so the unrepresented-clause fix is partial.
